title: timeline: a lookup `groupByField` renders one "[object Object]" group, and a text `groupByField` groups adjacent runs instead of bucketing by key
body:
Filing gate ①: a product defect measured at a public door (findings A-18, B-06, C-05, C-06). Filed by the triage seat (seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015, `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`), splitting objectstack-ai/objectstack#22722 (the maintainer's HotCRM browser pass, objectstack-ai/hotcrm#2058, measured on `@objectstack/*` 17.7.0). ⛔ Not a claim.

## Read on objectui `main` `ce991bd70f`

`packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.tsx`, `effectiveItems`:
- The group key is the raw `item[groupByField]` (about `:681`, kept as `group` at `:716`). The `groupByField` branch (about `:802`–`:816`) falls back to `String(value)`, so an expanded lookup becomes `[object Object]`. The header's CSS uppercases it.
- Title and description already go through `recordDisplayValueAt` (`:709`, `:713`); the group key does not.
- The items are sorted by start date only (about `:744`). `renderer.tsx` `groupAdjacent()` (about `:1512`) then merges only consecutive equal keys. That is right for date buckets and wrong for an explicit `groupByField`.

Measured on HotCRM: `groupByField: 'owner_id'` on the opportunity, event and task timelines, and `'crm_account'` on contracts, each render one group. `channel` renders DIGITAL 1, EMAIL 1, DIGITAL 1 ….

## Done when
- The group key is the field's display value, through `recordDisplayValueAt`. A lookup groups by the referenced record's name.
- With `groupByField` set, items are bucketed by key: one group per key, dates ordered within each. Date buckets are unchanged.
- Pins:
  - a lookup group key;
  - a text key whose rows interleave in date order;
  - CONTROL: a timeline with no `groupByField`.

`domain:ui` · p2.
